exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery)
outcome: Presence of IgA immune complexes on umbilical cord erythrocytes
Presence of IgG immune complexes on umbilical cord erythrocytes
Presence of IgM immune complexes on umbilical cord erythrocytes
C3d complement deposition on umbilical cord erythrocytes
cohort: The study included 34 umbilical cord blood samples from normal, full-term pregnancies (14 from vaginal deliveries and 20 from cesarean deliveries).
finding: IgG and IgM complexes are normally present on umbilical cord erythrocytes and are non-pathological, with a higher percentage of IgG complexes found on erythrocytes from vaginal deliveries compared to cesarean deliveries.
mod_finding: The percentage of IgG complexes was higher on erythrocytes from vaginal delivery samples compared to those from cesarean deliveries.
